sampling_model.design: I.i.d. superpopulation sampling from a fixed finite-stratum law.
sampling_model.treatment: The latent dose \(A_i\) is observed only through \(S_{i1}=A_i+U_{i1}\) and \(S_{i2}=A_i+U_{i2}\); the errors are independent, nonidentically distributed, potentially asymmetric, and may have characteristic-function zero sets.
sampling_model.overlap: The finite strata have masses at least \(p_{\min}\), and \(f_x(a)\ge\kappa\) on \(I\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The probability and signed marked channels are controlled by continuous integrated empirical contrasts on \(\mathcal C_*\). Entire-transform continuation and Sobolev recovery are profiled jointly, and an outward-rounded finite certificate approximates every continuum constraint to \(\zeta_n=o(r_n)\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The compact-support blind-replicate density estimator attains squared \(L^2\) risk of order \((\log\log n/\log n)^{2\beta}\), with a matching density lower bound.
The known-error continuous-treatment estimator admits pointwise asymptotic inference for the ADRF.

Theorems S11 and S12 give a uniform-in-treatment asymptotically linear representation and multiplier-bootstrap inference for the ADRF when the continuous treatment is observed without measurement error.
A latent-variable variational framework estimates a continuous-treatment ADRF under measurement error with neural density models.
Inverting finite complex Kotlarski moment tests gives a uniformly size-controlled latent-density confidence band without imposing completeness.
A multiplier-bootstrap density band is uniformly valid when the unknown error law is learned from auxiliary data or symmetric repeated measurements.
Wavelet deconvolution estimators attain minimax sup-norm density rates under a known convolution operator.
Testing affinity yields lower bounds on confidence-band width over nonparametric function classes.
Under weak unconfoundedness and positivity, the error-free ADRF is identified by the continuous-treatment g-formula.

body.tldr: The observed law contains two bilinear transform channels: an unmarked probability channel and an outcome-marked signed channel. Continuous integrated control of both channels on a moment-derived protected frequency square, followed by quantitative analytic continuation and Sobolev recovery, is conjectured to yield an honest simultaneous band for the ADRF with expected maximal width \(r_n\asymp(\log\log n/\log n)^{\beta-1/2}\). A terminating outward-rounded finite profile decodes rational certificate boxes into sets of full laws and evaluates their ADRFs by certified intervals, making the band operational without an empirical-grid inverse. A fixed-density, fixed-error Bernoulli marked experiment supplies the matching lower bound and isolates uncertainty about the causal curve rather than uncertainty about the treatment density.

project_justification.gap: Colangelo and Lee give uniform-in-treatment ADRF inference when treatment is measured without error, and known-error measurement-error methods give pointwise ADRF inference. Blind repeated-measurement methods identify and estimate an unmarked density, and robust Kotlarski methods invert finite complex moments for density bands. None gives an honest whole-curve ADRF band, a sharp expected-width modulus, or a fixed-nuisance marked converse when the two replicate errors are unknown, asymmetric, nonidentical, and allowed to have spectral zeros.
project_justification.niche: Compact dose support makes both the density transform and the signed marked transform entire. A common second-moment radius supplies a uniform nonvanishing neighborhood by \(|\varphi_j(t)|\ge1-|t|\sqrt{M_e}\), so the protected square is derived from a standard moment condition. The inferential object is a paired nonlinear quotient rather than a single density inverse.
project_justification.fill: The project derives the paired protected inverse at the sharp sup-norm exponent, embeds it in a continuously constrained confidence profile, decodes every retained rational box into represented full laws, certifies the resulting law-valued profile endpoints by outward interval evaluation with negligible inflation, and matches the upper width with Bernoulli marked alternatives that leave the full unmarked replicate law fixed.

body.related_work: Colangelo and Lee (2025), especially Supplementary Theorems S11 and S12 on pages 63--65 of the public manuscript, are the closest published uniform-in-treatment ADRF comparator: they derive a uniform asymptotically linear representation and multiplier-bootstrap inference over a compact treatment set when treatment is measured without error. Thus whole-curve ADRF inference itself is not the new obstacle; the obstacle is simultaneous inference after blind deconvolution with two unknown, nonidentical, asymmetric replicate errors. Huang and Zhang (2023) motivate the continuous-treatment measurement-error problem and derive pointwise ADRF inference when the error transform is known; their operator is not blind and their result is not simultaneous. Gao, Bondell, Huang, and Gong (2024) estimate a latent-treatment ADRF through a variational neural model, without a blind-replicate identification or honest-band theorem. Capitao-Miniconi, Gassiat, and Lehéricy (2025) provide the closest method exemplar: their continuous integrated analytic-polynomial contrast achieves a nearly parametric local transform error, analytic continuation yields an unmarked density rate, and a Legendre packet proves a compact-support density converse. The present target adds a signed marked channel, a quotient, supremum loss, honest band coverage, and a fixed-nuisance lower experiment. Kato, Sasaki, and Ura (2021) show how test inversion avoids fragile closed-form Kotlarski division, but their finite moments target an unmarked density and do not certify a continuum profile or a sharp width. Kato and Sasaki (2018, 2019) supply Gaussian and multiplier-bootstrap machinery for density and errors-in-variables regression bands under auxiliary, symmetric, or conventional spectral information. Neumann (2007) motivates integrated characteristic functions as continuous probability coordinates. Lounici and Nickl (2011), Genovese and Wasserman (2008), and Low (1997) inform the sup-norm packing and band-width reduction. The Colangelo--Lee comparison is informed-by rather than a claimed tightening; the only equivalence claim is the explicit error-free reduction in Theorem 9.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The protected inverse in Open-ended Question 4 is load-bearing. Its proof must keep the continuous forward error nearly parametric while analytic continuation amplifies only the stochastic error; inserting a spatial Jackson remainder into the forward tolerance recreates the rejected parent argument. The finite certificate must enclose the continuum constraints directly and may have pessimistic worst-case complexity. On the lower side, the same packet must preserve the Bernoulli range, strict Sobolev slack, fixed nuisance laws, and product-law total variation; failure of any one condition invalidates the claimed frontier.
body.honest_scope: The main frontier fixes \(\beta\), the support interval, all Sobolev radii, overlap constants, the outcome bound, and a common error second-moment radius. Error distributions remain unknown, nonidentical, asymmetric, and may have zero sets away from the moment-derived protected neighborhood. Adaptation to unknown smoothness or drifting channel severity is outside the theorem. When \(U_1=U_2=0\), Theorem 9 recovers the standard error-free g-formula.
